public_rationale: Contemporaneous scientific assessment and developer research describe safeguards that improve protection but retain material weaknesses. That supports the ordinary claim that prevention was not assured. It does not establish that prevention is impossible, that safeguards have no value, or that the eventual severity of incidents is wholly unknowable.
limitations: This is an assessment of available assurance, not proof that no secure design could exist.
Much of the evidence concerns safeguard bypass generally rather than this exact intrusion mechanism.
The unquantified statement about future severity is not separately graded.
